<details class="hub-details">
<summary>Evidence and current knowledge</summary>
## Why does it matter?

**Rationale:** The promoted fusion had 75 zero-nDCG sole-positive failures, and the released history made analogue transfer directly testable without target-response access.

**Research question:** [Can candidate-side semantic evidence improve query-only retrieval?](../questions/candidate-evidence.qmd); [When do promising signals fail?](../questions/failure-conditions.qmd); [How far can query-only routing go?](../questions/query-only-routing.qmd)

## How does it work?

**Hypothesis:** Fine-grained query analogues will transfer enough candidate evidence to explain or recover a material share of the 75 failures.

Freeze the 75-case cohort, screen historical analogues without target qrels, run leave-one-query-out lexical and dense transfer, and separate fusion dilution from missing evidence.

Any run comparison below is partitioned by ledger evaluation scope.

## What do we know?

**Outcome:** `negative`

Query analogues rarely identify the official positive: only 11 of 75 had strong or corroborated pre-qrel evidence, and 54 of 75 had no top-ten positive from either promoted component.

**Decision:** `reject`

Do not treat ordinary query-neighbor transfer or another static fusion weight as the missing ranking signal; test stronger response-evidence reranking instead.

Rationale provenance: `contemporaneous`.
</details>

<details class="hub-details">
<summary>Limits and readiness</summary>
Development-only post-hoc audit. Target candidate responses and assessor rationale are unavailable; historical attempts are not correctness labels; the multi-representation transfer sweep is an unreproduced exploratory receipt, and its best setting is not an unbiased estimate.

Development results do not establish hidden-test effectiveness.
</details>

<details class="hub-details">
<summary>Relationships and technical details</summary>
## Authored decision notes

The diagnostic separates two actionable conditions. In 21 cases one component
already ranked the official positive in its top ten and equal reciprocal-rank
fusion vetoed it. In the other 54, neither component supplied a top-ten signal,
so reweighting those same lists cannot recover the positive without new
evidence.
